description: Frozen cross-language golden vectors for the uniflag v2 binary protocol (docs/protocol.md; docs/v2-plan.md M6). The Rust conformance suite (proto/tests/golden_vectors.rs) and the C# plugin suite load these exact files; neither side generates its own fixtures. Regenerate only via just golden-regen.

reading.raw: type byte, then payload, then CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE (poly 0x1021, init 0xFFFF, no reflection, xorout 0) computed over type+payload and appended little-endian
reading.wire: COBS-encoded raw followed by a single 0x00 delimiter; canonical Cheshire-Baker Listing 1 encoding, meaning the encoder always terminates with a group header
reading.negative: strip the single trailing 0x00 delimiter, then run the remaining bytes through the decode pipeline (COBS decode, then CRC check, then typed parse); it must fail with the error class named by the vector
reading.stream: split on 0x00 delimiters, run every non-empty segment through the decode pipeline, drop segments that fail; the surviving packets must equal expected_packets exactly and in order

vectors.name: hello
vectors.purpose: host->device handshake open carrying the protocol version

vectors.name: hello_ack
vectors.purpose: device->host handshake reply: protocol version, 32x32 panel, fw_version 2.0.0-test

vectors.name: button_event_short
vectors.purpose: device->host short press of button 0 (brightness up)

vectors.name: frame

packet.note: payload is the 3072 pattern bytes; compare against raw[1..3073] verbatim

vectors.purpose: full 32x32 RGB888 frame; deterministic piecewise payload (byte i): i<256 -> 0 if i%8==0 else i; i<512 -> 0xFF; i<1024 -> (i*7)%256; i<1342 -> (i%253)+1; else i%256. Contains zero bytes, a 257-byte 0xFF run (byte 255 is already 0xFF, then 256..=511), and non-zero runs longer than 254 bytes, so COBS group handling is exercised end to end

vectors.name: cobs_boundary_254
vectors.purpose: raw form ends in exactly 254 non-zero bytes immediately after a zero byte, so a canonical (Cheshire-Baker Listing 1) COBS encoder emits a full 0xFF group followed by a trailing 0x01 group header before the delimiter. The Wikipedia cobsEncode example omits that trailing 0x01; an encoder ported from it produces a wire one byte shorter and must fail the byte-exact comparison against this vector. Type byte 0x7E is unassigned, so receivers parse this packet as unknown and ignore it. Exact raw bytes, re-derivable: [0x7E, 0x51, tweak, 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, .., 0xFC, crc_lo, crc_hi] where tweak is the smallest value in 0x00..=0xFF for which neither CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE byte of the whole preceding sequence is zero; in this frozen file tweak = 0x00, giving 252 ascending pattern bytes + 2 CRC bytes = 254 zero-free trailing bytes after the 0x00 at raw offset 3

vectors.name: bad_crc
vectors.purpose: brightness packet whose payload byte was corrupted after the CRC was computed; COBS decodes cleanly, the CRC check must reject

vectors.name: truncated
vectors.purpose: COBS group header promises 4 data bytes but only 2 are present before the delimiter; the COBS decoder must reject

vectors.name: embedded_zero_garbage
vectors.purpose: a 0x00 inside COBS group data, which a valid encoder never produces; the COBS decoder must reject

vectors.name: wrong_length_known_type
vectors.purpose: valid CRC, known type Frame (0x02), but a 5-byte payload instead of 3072; the typed layer must reject

vectors.name: resync
vectors.purpose: garbage bytes containing no delimiter, then a lone 0x00, then hello.wire and brightness.wire verbatim; a decoder walking the stream must drop the garbage segment and recover exactly the two embedded packets in order
